title: fix(agents): keep private runtime entries out of saved context
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Legacy or unauthenticated runtime-context entries can leak into compaction summaries and saved CLI session notes when their persisted rows lack producer metadata.

## User Impact

Reserved `openclaw.runtime-context` entries remain private when older transcripts are read, including entries without carrier metadata and entries explicitly opted out of provider replay. Conversation and durable-note retention rules stay intact. Stored history is not rewritten and no migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime-context cutover made the privacy classifier use the stricter provider-carrier recognizer. That conflated hiding private content with granting provider replay authority. This is fail-closed hiding: reserved runtime-context custom messages stay private even when they have no producer or replay authority; the separate provider-authority checks remain strict. It protects persisted transcripts from before the cutover as well as unauthenticated entries.

Main now seeds CLI history through the canonical producer (`f40a007daffa`) and checks typed completion events in `internalEvents` (`31412680307a`). This rebase takes both peer-fixed test files unchanged from main. The remaining change is the privacy classifier, its token-sanitization regression, and the transcript-hygiene documentation.

## Evidence

Post-rebase proof passed on Linux via Crabbox (Node 24.21.0). The remote source was verified against the exact three-file patch and source hashes for `884f4c3f2c60` before testing:

- Token-sanitize, CLI session-history, and sessions-send child-coordination: **78 tests passed in 170 seconds**.
- Transcript-hygiene coverage: **232 tests across 10 files passed in 76 seconds**.
- Compaction families: **226 tests across 18 files passed in 85 seconds**, including the runtime-context custom-message exclusion from generated summaries.

The two peer-fixed test files exactly match main at the rebase base, `67ab6f3104fd`.

The retained three files are byte-for-byte identical to the previously reviewed version. Prior Linux proof reproduced the original compaction failure, then passed three repetitions of the requested files, the hygiene and compaction families, and `check-changed` (1,343 seconds, including core types, all 27 core test-type graphs, lint, dead-export and import-cycle checks). Independent P2 review and explicit boundary lint passed. That proof remains prior-head evidence; the requested post-rebase runs are recorded above.

No filters, existing assertions, timeouts, retries, skips, baselines, schemas, permissions, imports or exports were changed. No GitHub CI dispatches or reruns were used.
